title: 00 — AI Engineering: Index

00 — AI Engineering: Index

The one idea: an AI application is ordinary software with one unusual component, a model that is powerful, probabilistic and steerable by text. Everything in this set is about building around that component: giving it the right context and tools, keeping it safe, measuring whether it works, and choosing a stack you can run.

1. What this set is

A practical guide to building generative AI applications: chatbots, MCP tool servers, agents and voice assistants, with the security and evaluation work that makes them shippable. Each note explains how the thing works, what to use to build it, and the mistakes that sink real projects.

It builds on notes that already exist:

Already covered Where
Prompting, structured output, RAG, agents, LLM security basics, cost LLM Engineering & RAG
How transformers and attention work Neural Networks and Transformers from Scratch
Fine-tuning and LoRA Fine-Tuning and LoRA
Hybrid search and the Databricks AI stack The Databricks AI Stack
OWASP lists, tool pinning, least agency Securing Agents and MCP Tools

Runnable examples use only the Python standard library or numpy, with stand-in "models", so they show the mechanics offline. Real API code (the Claude SDK for Python and C#, MCP SDKs, voice frameworks) is marked not run, because the build environment had no packages or API keys. That code follows the official documentation as checked on 2026-10-27.

2. Chapter map

# Chapter What you get from it
01 How Generative AI Works Tokens, context windows, sampling, embeddings, model families, choosing a model
02 Calling Models in Practice Messages, system prompts, streaming, structured output, tools, caching, errors, cost (Python and C#)
03 Building a Chatbot Architecture, conversation state, grounding with citations, human handoff, channels, deployment
04 Building MCP Servers and Clients Tools, resources and prompts, transports, the 2026-07-28 stateless spec, SDKs, connecting to models
05 Agents and Multi-Agent Systems The agent loop, when not to build one, frameworks, A2A, memory, human approval
06 Voice Assistants VAD, STT, LLM, TTS, speech-to-speech, turn detection, barge-in, latency budgets, telephony
07 Generative AI Security Threat model, injection, output handling, data leakage, guardrails, red teaming
08 Evaluation and Observability Eval sets, graders, LLM judges, regression gates, tracing, cost and quality monitoring
09 Choosing a Stack and a Build Plan .NET and Python stacks, reference architectures, step-by-step builds for each app type

3. Reading order

  1. Everyone: 01 → 02, then LLM Engineering & RAG.
  2. Then the app you want to build: a chatbot (03), tools for any AI client (04), an agent (05), or a voice assistant (06).
  3. Before shipping anything: 07 and 08.
  4. To plan a project: 09.

The AI Engineer track puts this set into a beginner-to-senior path.
